Subject: Immediate actions: Split-region reachability impacting US & APAC — recommended reroute steps

Hi Jenna / Lodestone ops team,

Quick note from Infra: we're seeing a split-region reachability issue affecting a subset of US and APAC egress paths to our hosted inference cluster (regions us-west-2 and ap-southeast-1). Impact is intermittent 5–20% request failures and elevated tail latency for customers pinned to those routes. EU region remains healthy.

We recommend the following minimal-impact steps you can take immediately to reduce user-facing errors while we remediate on the networking plane:

1) DNS / Edge: set your client to prefer eu-east (api.eu.redwood.com) as the primary endpoint for requests until we clear the incident. This reduces cross-region egress exposure.
2) SDK override: if you use the Redwood SDK, set REDWOOD_API_REGION=eu in your environment and restart any long-lived worker processes.
3) Model pinning: if you rely on large models, pin to a smaller-latency variant in eu (we recommend rwd-llm-medium-1-eu) to avoid model-download fallthroughs.
4) Retry policy: implement idempotent retries with exponential backoff (max 2 retries, jitter). Avoid aggressive concurrency spikes during failover.
5) Observability: if you can, send a short sample request id and timestamp to ops@redwood.com — that helps us correlate at the edge.

Attached is a short checklist for your SREs (reroute_checklist.pdf) and an API fallback snippet (api-fallback-instructions.txt). We're actively working the network path with the cloud provider; ETA for primary fix is unclear but we will update every 90 minutes.

Immediate ask: please reply with a one-line ack and whether you'd like Redwood to initiate an automatic failover (we can enable traffic steering for you from our side — requires consent).

Apologies for the disruption. We'll keep you posted.

— Priyom
Priyom Das

Acknowledged. Infra on-call here — quick notes: 
1) Control-plane steering: we have a traffic-steer toggle that reroutes new requests at the edge to eu; existing streaming connections will not be preserved and will see a single connection reset. We will coordinate a 5-minute maintenance window with Lodestone before toggling.
2) Auth: no token changes required. Authentication is global; clients will continue to use the same API keys. We will surface a brief outage during the switch (expected < 2 minutes for most requests, but we will conservatively communicate 5 minutes).
3) Rollback: automatic rollback if error rate increases beyond 10% vs baseline for 10m.

Planned ops timeline (subject to Lodestone approval):
- 09:15 PT: Lodestone canary SDK override to 5% of traffic.
- 09:30 PT: Redwood-enabled steering for Lodestone (5–10 minute window).
- 10:00 PT: Observe, then increase to 50% if green.

I will be on the call and will post step-by-step commands. Attaching a short run-note template to append to the postmortem.

Subject: Incident update & postmortem link — Split-region reachability (US/APAC)

Hi Jenna / Lodestone ops,

Thanks for working with us yesterday. Short summary and next artifacts: 

- What happened: transient split in cloud provider egress that affected a subset of US and APAC edge paths. This caused elevated 5xx and increased tail latency for customers routed through those edges.
- What we did: coordinated an assisted failover for Lodestone at 09:30 PT (we did a staged steer; initial window <2m, increased to 50% after 30m). SDK override canaries were used to validate.
- Impact to you: brief connection resets during the steer; no data loss; client API keys unchanged.
- Next steps: full postmortem is available here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-postmortem-LOD-4821

We're keeping the postmortem draft live — Monica has the timeline and Ben attached run-notes. We'll add an RCA and mitigation recommendations (additional telemetry at the edge, enhanced cross-region health checks) by EOD Friday.

If you'd like a 30-minute walkthrough of the postmortem with your SREs, Vanessa is lined up to host that session next week.

Appreciate the partnership and patient testing during the steer.

Best,
